subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add Mission Control workspace-wide editing and/or host system filesystem browsing beyond the current bootstrap-file editor and read-only workspace browser?
rationale: The remaining request changes which user and host files operator clients can read or mutate, and current policy prioritizes safe defaults plus explicit security decisions for broad filesystem surfaces.

options.title: Workspace-Only First
options.body: Use the existing read-only `agents.workspace.list/get` slice as the safe base, settle workspace write/delete/move/upload in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368, and defer system filesystem browsing.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap Editing Only
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing limited to core bootstrap files while allowing read-only workspace browsing where already approved.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Open a separate security design for host filesystem browsing with explicit operator opt-in, authorization, auditing, limits, and non-destructive defaults.

recommendation.title: Workspace-Only First
recommendation.body: Use the existing read-only `agents.workspace.list/get` slice as the safe base, settle workspace write/delete/move/upload in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368, and defer system filesystem browsing.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the partial read-only workspace API and mobile browser commits and are the clearest owner for the remaining security/product boundary.
